amendments.change: seeds 3 -> 5, using the NB26 seed set [101,211,307,401,503]
amendments.reason: NB26 measured recovery-seed variance exceeding selection-method variance (deep AWBIR 47% seed vs 10% method); 3 unblocked seeds per method is underpowered for that variance structure, and sharing NB26 seeds makes the two experiments directly comparable.

amendments.change: primary test Kruskal-Wallis -> Friedman blocked by seed (Kendall W reported); Kruskal-Wallis retained as an unblocked secondary
amendments.reason: every method is recovered under the identical seed set, so the design is matched-block; blocking removes the dominant seed variance instead of letting it mask method effects.

amendments.change: outcomes split: units to family-F1 threshold, and units to threshold AND benign-false-alert guard; guard-binding frequency reported
amendments.reason: NB26 shows shallow minimal-recovery benign_to_attack near the 0.05 guard, so one combined outcome would conflate slow recovery with guard violation.

amendments.change: secondary continuous outcome added: mean family macro-F1 across units (AUC)
amendments.reason: units-to-threshold is coarse and censored; the AUC uses the whole curve.

amendment.primary_outcome: recovery units (passes over the frozen 10% subset) to tau
amendment.tau: family macro-F1 >= 0.95 x plateau, plateau = median across ALL methods and seeds of the final-unit family macro-F1
amendment.censoring: runs not reaching tau by E_MAX recorded as E_MAX+1 (censored)
amendment.G6a_pass: Friedman p<0.05 (blocked by seed) AND median spread >= 1 unit, in >=1 architecture
amendment.G6b_pass: saber_v2 strictly lowest median units in >=1 architecture, within 1 unit elsewhere
